item.title: DNA testing of fecal samples reveals greater gliders eat wider variety of plants than previously thought
item.description: Identifying the favorite snacks of one of Australia's cutest animals no longer needs to rely on guesswork or picking apart their poop, according to University of the Sunshine Coast research. Although the shortened title of her latest paper is "The future is faeces," associate professor Dominique Potvin and colleagues want to make the task less of a hands-on, hit-and-miss job. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: The winner of this year’s Nobel Prize in Literature is Canada’s Anne Carson, an essayist and classicist who brings a modern twist to mysticism and antiquity in her writings about love, desire and despair. The 76-year-old won “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”, the Swedish Academy said on Thursday. Carson is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: NSW protects first pink lakes: governments buy Pulgamurtie Station
item.description: The acquisition of Pulgamurtie Station in New South Wales, covering 74,000 hectares of unique landscapes, aims to protect the area's stunning pink lakes and vulnerable wildlife. This initiative not only prioritizes Aboriginal cultural heritage but also fosters diverse ecosystems vital for local species. Future plans include opportunities for recreational activities like birdwatching and scenic drives, supporting Australia's goal to expand protected areas. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
